newsitem.title: FRANCE: 1998 deficit will not exceed three pct - Jospin.
newsitem.headline: 1998 deficit will not exceed three pct - Jospin.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Friday the government aimed to have a public deficit next year which did not exceed three percent of gross domestic product.
He also said efforts to reduce public spending would be stepped up in 1998.

He said managing the budget next year would be "a little more difficult" given that the government would not have the benefit of a one-off transfer of funds from France Telecom, which helped reduce the deficit this year.
The transfer of 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom to cover future pension liabilities reduced the deficit this year by 0.45 percent of GDP.
But he said in an interview with RTL radio that the government aimed to curb the deficit next year, both to prevent a new increase in debt and to meet its European commitments.
"Our target is not to exceed a deficit of three percent for all public accounts in 1998," he said.
The government would aim at the same time not to brake growth and work to promote jobs.
Asked about whether the reduction in spending would be stepped up in 1998, he said, "as regards government spending, of course".
